text:
1. INTRODUCTION
Fire and Smoke Detection System (FSDS)
The Fire and Smoke Detection System (FSDS) is a critical safety feature designed
to detect and alert the presence of fire and smoke within the Air-Conditioned coach. Below mentioned are the key details of the system:
I. Design: The FSDS is designed for very early warning for smoke/fire incidents
in air-conditioned coaches. II. Sampling Nozzles and Pipe Network: These include Sampling Nozzles,
capillary tubes and PVC pipeline strategically placed throughout the coaches
to collect air samples to analyze the existence of fire/ smoke. III. Control Panel / Fire Detection Panel and Power Panel: This panel, available
in each coach, contains the Aspirating Smoke Detection Unit and Power panel
for 24V battery backup and DC-DC Convertor to convert 110VDC to 24VDC. The Aspiration smoke detection Unit collects air samples from throughout the
coach, analyses in the detection panel for existence of fire/smoke and initiates
appropriate responses. IV. Alarms: Audible and visual alarms alert passengers and train staff to the
presence of smoke or fire, enabling swift evacuation and response. V. Automatic Response: The FSDS has provision of integration with the train's
braking system to automatically stop the train in case of a fire emergency. Fire Detection and Suppression System (FDSS)
It is an advanced safety system designed to detect the presence of fire/smoke and
automatically suppress it to prevent the spread and minimize damage. I.

Detection: The system uses point type smoke detectors, point type heat
detectors and linear heat detection cable placed suitably inside the coach. II. Alarm:
a) When the smoke is detected through smoke detector, it will raise pre- alarm
in detection panel. b) When the heat/fire is detected through heat detector, it will raise fire- alarm
in detection panel. c) When the heat/fire is detected through LHD cable, it will raise fire- alarm in
detection panel. III. Suppression: The Power Cars / Pantry coaches are equipped with a High
Pressure Water Mist Fire Suppression System. In case of a fire, alarm raised
by detection unit, the system is designed to suppress the fire and prevent it
from spreading.

Documentation Structure of Maintenance Manual
To simplify the maintenance instructions, the Maintenance Manual for FSDS and
FDSS is divided into two volumes:
Volume-1: This volume contains details of the FSDS & FDSS unit in Vande Bharat
and Amrit Bharat Coaches.
Volume-2: This volume contains details of the FSDS & FDSS unit in ICF and LHB
Coaches.

4.1.1. Technical Details
An Aspiration Type Automatic Smoke / Fire Detection with Alarm System gives early
warning against any smoke/fire.
In this system, Sampling pipe/ Sampling points network is designed to cover entire
coach’s passenger area including lavatories, doorway & gangway of coach. A system
of intake pipes with defined sampling orifices performs active air sampling and sends
the smoke levels to the Central Control Unit (CCU).
Working Principle of FSDS System
Air is drawn into the pipe network through the sampling points (Aspiration System)
from a close surrounding and traverses to a very sensitive smoke detector consisting
of an aspirator, detection chamber, dual stage filter and necessary networking card.
The negative pressure of an aspirator helps in drawing ambient air to a detection
chamber where scattering of light occurs and detection of smoke takes place.
FSDS system works on the principle of actively drawing air samples from the coach
through sampling points and directed to a detection chamber in the detector. The
presence of smoke in the sample air results in the scattering of the laser that is
instantly detected by a configuration of light receiver. Depending upon the smoke level,
an output signal is processed and displayed on the detector chamber. The system is
designed as a multi-level alarm system with each level of smoke threshold resulting in
a different alarm warning for the passengers.

section: Visual Inspection - Pipe Network and Sampling Points
text:
Visual Inspection of Pipe Network and Sampling Points

Procedure: Check the Piping Network near the FDS Panel and Sampling Points for any damage or deposition of dust or soot.

Acceptable Criteria:
1. There should be no breakage of Pipe Network near FDS Panel
2. No Pipe joint should be loose
3. Sampling points should be free from blockage
4. No dust or soot deposition on sampling points
5. Safety covers of sampling points should be intact

Note: Check for physical damage, loose joints, blockages, and contamination. Clean sampling points if dust/soot found.

Smoke Test Procedure (FSDS)

Procedure: By simulating smoke at the farthest sampling point, check the response of the system for all levels of Alarms.

Steps:
1. Simulate smoke at the farthest sampling point using a smoke generator
2. Check system response for each alarm level:

   Stage 1 - Alert (0.35 ± 0.05 %obs/m, 20 sec delay):
   - Flasher Light should activate on fire detection panel of affected coach
   
   Stage 2 - Action (0.6 ± 0.05 %obs/m, 30 sec delay):
   - Strobe Light with Hooter should activate
   - Public Announcement should trigger
   
   Stage 3 - Fire (1.6 ± 0.05 %obs/m, 45 sec delay):
   - Brake Application should occur (verify by LED on Display Panel)

3. Verify all components respond correctly:
   - Flasher Light (Alert stage)
   - Strobe Light and Hooter (Action stage)
   - Public Announcement (Action stage)
   - Brake Application LED on panel (Fire stage)

The system should function with Alarm and Subsequent actions including Flasher Light, Strobe Light, Hooter, Public Announcement, and Brake Application.

Acceptable Criteria: All alarms trigger at correct thresholds with correct indications at each stage. Brake application confirmed by LED on Display Panel.

section: ICF Maintenance - Air Flow and Data Download
text:
Maintenance Procedure - ICF Coaches: Air Flow and Data Download

1. Download data log and check for any fault. If any fault, attend it.
2. Check the airflow reading. It should be within the range, i.e. Fn ± 20%, where Fn is the normal airflow value.
   - If less than Fn - 20%, clean the filter and re-check.
   - If still less than Fn - 20%, flush the pipeline with a vacuum cleaner/blower.
   - If still less, seek further guidance from the Supplier/OEM.
3. Check Air Flow value through OEM software.
4. Check the intactness of the power supply input voltage from the DC power supply to the detector and battery voltage.
5. Battery voltage check: Ensure battery is charged and holding voltage. Replace if defective.

Note: Please refer Para 4.1.3 Sr. No. 6 for checking Air Flow procedure details.

text:
5.1.1. Technical Details
The System is known as Fire Detection and Suppression System (FDSS), it is an
integration of two systems one is Fire detection and another one is Fire suppression /
extinguishing system. The Fire Detection System consists of Fire and Smoke Detectors placed suitably
inside the Generator area/pantry area. The Detectors are connected in a redundant
loop to the control module. The Control module is connected to an Audio-Visual Sounder beacon for Alarm in
case of a fire. The Fire Suppression System works on the Principle of High Pressure Water Mist
System
Principle of High Pressure Water Mist System
The most important effects of fire fighting with water mist are the cooling and oxygen
displacement effect. Through the atomization of water under high pressure, the
reaction surface available for the cooling process is significantly enlarged in
comparison to conventional low pressure systems. The water mist generated has a
total surface area, at least 100 times greater than a conventional sprinkler. The FDSS consists of water cylinders and a nitrogen cylinder, which are the source of
the pressurized water mist system. FDSS System has Heat Detectors and Smoke
Detectors. Smoke Detectors will provide pre-alarm, and after pre-alarm, manual activation of the
system is done through an activation switch provided on the control panel. Heat Detector provides fire alarm as well as automatic actuation of Fire Suppression
System.

title: Maintenance Manual for FSDS and FDSS Volume-2 (LHB & ICF Coaches)
text:
On receiving the Fire Alarm (through Heat Detectors/LHD Cable), an
automatic fire suppression system is operated. Fire detection unit constantly monitors and controls the fire protection system and is
also protected by a UPS with battery backup. The Control unit displays the ready
status, relevant faults and alarms. The water mist system is activated by an electrically
operated solenoid valve/magnetic valve on the nitrogen cylinder. If a fire is detected, a message is sent accordingly to the fire detection evaluation unit
and the generator cars vehicle control system, after which ventilation is shut down and
the fuel supply to the engines cut off. Visual and acoustic alarms are activated in the
guards’ compartment.

section: Next, perform a mechanical inspection of the magnetic valve (to do this put back
text:
8. Next, perform a mechanical inspection of the magnetic valve (to do this put back
the solenoid):
To perform a mechanical function test, a conventional Allen key as well as a lock
nut with vent hole is required.
a. Activate the valve electronically for two to three seconds, then switch off the
current or deactivate manual activation.
b. Undo the vent screw using the Allen key, turning it through half a rotation,
which will vent the valve area involved, causing the valve to close audibly. The
pressure, however, will remain in the valve outlet.
c. By carefully undoing the lock nut by about half a turn, then vent the valve outlet.
A short, audible emission of gas signals that the valve has opened correctly
as a result of electrical or manual activation. This escape of gas, however,

should cease immediately, otherwise the valve has not closed properly. If that
happens, do not remove the lock nut.
d. If the valve does not close, then it must be replaced. To do this, empty the
container through the valve outlet by turning the lock nut by no more than half
a turn. Secure the container appropriately before emptying.
e. If the valve is working properly, then screw up the vent screw again so that it
seals.
f. Return the system to its functional state.

6. PREVENTION OF FIRE
A. Coaches:
● All protective equipment such as fuses, contactors, MCBs etc. should be
intact and with proper rating. No bypassing and paralleling to be done
● Fire extinguishers as per guidelines with proper validity to be provided. ● Fire detection and alarm system provided in the coaches must be in
working condition
● Thermal scanning of Power panels of all coaches on load to done as per
extant guideline
● FDSS (Fire Detection and Suppression System) provided in pantry cars
should be in working condition and magnet valve for operating the
suppression. ● FSDS (Fire Smoke Detection System) should be in working condition. The angle cock connecting the penalty brake application should not be in
isolated condition. ● WSP should be in working order. ● Only metal (preferably stainless-steel) dustbins should be provided in
coaches. ● Garbage evacuation to be ensured at designated stations. ● Escorting staff should be properly trained and counseled for handling fire
incidents. ● Cleaning of LHB ACP panels
B. Pantry / Power Cars:
● FDSS (Fire Detection and Suppression System) provided in Power
Cars/Pantry Car should be in working condition. ● Leakage/Seepage of Lube and fuel oil in the engine room should be
arrested before putting in service. ● All safety equipment including sensors should be in working condition
● Radiator as well as side body filters to be cleaned properly.

title: Maintenance Manual for FSDS and FDSS Volume-2 (LHB & ICF Coaches)
section: PREVENTION OF FIRE + POST FIRE MAINTENANCE
text:
● Thermal scanning of power panels of Power Cars on load to done as per
extant guideline. ● Escorting staff should be counseled and trained
● Engine room and panel room should be dry.

7. POST FIRE MAINTENANCE
● After discharge, allow for appropriate holding time before ventilating the hazard
space.
● Always have backup portable fire extinguishers on hand for use in the unlikely
event of fire re-ignition.
● Ventilate the hazard area thoroughly by forced ventilation or by opening doors
and windows.
● Inspect that all fires have been extinguished and that there are no localized hot
spots or other sources of re-ignition present.

Caution:
● Ensure the fire is completely extinguished before ventilating the hazard space.
● Ventilate thoroughly or use a self-contained breathing apparatus before
entering.
● For areas with sensitive electronic equipment, recovery activities should begin
immediately after system discharge and the area is secured from fire re-
ignition. This will help protect electronic assets from possible damage.
Note: In case of fire incidence, detailed investigation/inspection is to be done
jointly with OEM as per the condition of the system.

8. Do’s & Don’ts
Do
● Use appropriate PPEs.
● Follow the prescribed inspection, maintenance and testing schedule for
the system.
● Proper record keeping of the system.
● Check the indication LEDs in the control/detection panel.
● Ensure that smoke is detected by the aspiration sampling point when it is
cleared of blockage due to vandalism or dust/dirt accumulation.
● Ensure that no smoke/fire source is present in the coach if an alarm/alert
indication is observed.
Don’t
● Remove or connect the wire/connections when the system is powered up
● Hard reset the system for resetting the alarm.
● Use Solvents for cleaning.
● Ignore re-occurring faults.
● Allow unqualified/untrained personnel to operate/test/service the system

WAGNER TITANUS PRO-SENS Automatic Smoke & Fire Detection System

Wagner Group GmbH manufactures the TITANUS PRO-SENS aspirating smoke detection system for railway coaches. The TITANUS PRO-SENS is one of the five OEM variants approved by RDSO for use in Indian Railway FSDS installations in AC coaches.

The Wagner system, like other FSDS variants, uses aspiration-based smoke detection with a pipe network sampling air from passenger areas, lavatories, doorways, and gangways. The aspirated air passes through a detection chamber where laser scattering technology detects smoke particles.

- Stage 1 (Alert): 0.35 ± 0.05 %obs/m, 20 second delay
- Stage 2 (Action): 0.6 ± 0.05 %obs/m, 30 second delay
- Stage 3 (Fire): 1.6 ± 0.05 %obs/m, 45 second delay, triggers automatic brake application

Maintenance and testing procedures for the Wagner system follow the standard IRCAMTECH maintenance manual guidelines applicable to all OEM variants.

1. INTRODUCTION
Fire and Smoke Detection System (FSDS)
The Fire and Smoke Detection System (FSDS) is a critical safety feature designed to detect and alert the presence of fire and smoke within the Vande Bharat Chaircar Coaches. Below mentioned are the key details of the system:
I. Design: The FSDS is designed for very early warning for smoke/fire incidents in air-conditioned coaches.
II. Sampling Nozzles and Pipe Network: These include sampling nozzles, capillary tubes, and pipelines. They are strategically placed throughout the coaches to collect air samples to analyze the existence of fire/smoke.
III. Control Panel / Fire Detection Panel and Power Panel: This panel, available in each coach, contains the Aspirating Smoke Detection Unit and Power panel for 24V battery backup and DC-DC Convertor to convert 110VDC to 24VDC. The Aspiration smoke detection Unit collects air samples from throughout the coach, analyses in the detection panel for existence of fire/smoke and initiates appropriate responses.
IV. Alarms: Audible and visual alarms alert passengers and train staff to the presence of smoke or fire, enabling swift evacuation and response.
V. Automatic Response: The FSDS has provision of integration with the train's braking system to automatically stop the train in case of a fire emergency.

Fire Detection and Suppression System (FDSS)
It is an advanced safety system designed to detect the presence of fire/smoke and automatically suppress it to prevent the spread and minimize damage. The FDSS employs an aerosol-based fire suppression system in Vande Bharat and Amrit Bharat coaches.

Documentation Structure: Volume-1 covers FSDS & FDSS for Vande Bharat and Amrit Bharat Coaches. Volume-2 covers ICF and LHB Coaches.

4. FIRE AND SMOKE DETECTION SYSTEM (FSDS)
4.1. Aspiration Type Automatic Smoke / Fire Detection with Alarm System for Vande Bharat Chaircar Coaches (Ver. 2.0)
N&S HOCHIKI - FIRE & SMOKE DETECTION SYSTEM

4.1.1. Technical Details
An Aspiration Type Automatic Smoke / Fire Detection with Alarm System is used in the active fire protection of Vande Bharat Coaches. This system consists of a high-sensitivity Aspirating Smoke Detection Unit connected to a network of pipes. These pipes draw air from various points throughout the coach to the detection unit for continuous analysis using the HOCHIKI FIRELINK 25 unit.

Key features:
- Aspirating Smoke Detection: Actively draws air samples through a pipe network from multiple points within the coach and analyzes them for the presence of smoke particles.
- Laser-Based Detection: Utilizes advanced laser technology to detect the presence of smoke particles in the air samples, enabling early detection of even small amounts of smoke.
- Multiple Alarm Levels: Configurable alarm thresholds allow for multiple levels of alarm sensitivity, providing graded alerts depending on the concentration of smoke detected.
- Self-Diagnostic: Monitors the operation of the sampling system, providing information about electrical discontinuity, obstruction of the sampling system, system disability, or faults.

Components: Aspirating Smoke Detection Unit (FIRELINK 25), Fire Panel (LCD, keypad, data storage, LED indicators), 25-meter sampling pipe network, Photoelectric smoke detectors (point-type) in electrical cabinets, Heat Activated Sampling Points (HASP) in pantry sections.

Power Supply: 110 ± 30% VDC input, converted to 24 ± 6 VDC for FSDS operation.

   b. LED indication on the Aspirating Smoke Detection Unit.
   c. The TCMS Driver Display Unit in the Driver Console/Desk in DTC will display the fire detection indication symbol in Red Color and the corresponding coach number diagnostic message.
   d. The MIN 1 FD lamp at the MCP Unit Display Panel of the Driver Console/Desk in DTC will be illuminated.
   e. The FDS buzzer will be activated in the Hooter/Buzzer Panel of the Driver Console/Desk in DTC.
   f. The buzzer in the passenger area will not be activated unless it is enabled by the loco pilot.
   g. The buzzer in the passenger area can be enabled by the loco pilot by Switching-On the FDS ENABLE switch at the MCP Unit Display Panel of the Driver Console/Desk in DTC.

Note: When an aspiration sampling point is cleared of obstruction due to vandalism or dust/dirt accumulation, check the smoke detection for the cleared sampling point to ensure its proper functioning.

text:
4.1.2.3. Over Heated Wire Test
A. General
1. This test conforms to BS 6266 with minimal amount of PVC coated wire test, and is designed to verify that the detector responds in an acceptable time to a slowly developing fire scenario.

B. Test Equipment
1. PVC coated wire: 800 mm of PVC-coated copper wire (10 strands of 0.1 mm) firmly stretched and attached approximately 25 mm directly below the nearest sampling point (or HASP).
2. Transformer: 6 Volt output transformer.

C. Procedure
1. The wire shall be connected to the 6V output terminal of the transformer.
2. Ensure that the wire is attached approximately 25 mm directly below the nearest sampling point.
3. Energize the wire for 60 seconds.
4. De-energize the wire after 60 seconds.
5. The system must respond within 60 seconds after cessation (de-energizing) of the heat source.
6. If the system does not respond within 60 seconds, investigate the cause and repeat the test.

Note: This test is conducted during SS1/SS2/SS3 maintenance schedules.

title: Maintenance Manual for FSDS and FDSS Volume-1 (Vande Bharat & Amrit Bharat Coaches)
text:
4.1.2.4. Replacement of Dust Separator / Filter of Aspirating Smoke Detection Unit
The dust separator condition can be checked using the Dust Separator Test in the Miscellaneous Tab of the remote software 'Detector settings' screen which gives a percentage reading of dust separator efficiency. When this level drops to 80% the detector will signal a fault and the dust separator will need replacing.

Dust Separator / Filter Replacement Procedure:
1. Make sure that the power supply to the Automatic Smoke / Fire Detection System is switched off.
2. Remove the front cover of the detection unit by removing the cover-fixing screws.
3. Pull out the existing filter from the filter slot.
4. Slide the replacement filter in so that the 'Direction of flow' arrow printed on the carton duplicates that on the 'Direction of flow' label beside the filter slot.
5. Refit the front cover by cover-fixing screws.

Caution:
1. As dust contained in the dust separators may expose maintenance personnel to a 'Nuisance Dust' hazard, it is strongly recommended that suitable masks and protective clothing (PPE) be worn when changing filters.
2. Used separators/filters are not intended for re-use and should be disposed of.

2. Internal cleaning should be done by vacuuming the inside of the detection panel.
3. Do not use any solvents for cleaning.

2. Open the Hochiki FireLink 25 configuration tool software on the computer.
3. Select the menu options View > Event Log or click on the Event Log Symbol.
4. A screen will be displayed in the software showing the time and date of each event stored in the log along with its general description.
5. Press the Print button and select the Microsoft Print to PDF option and press the OK button to save the data log file at your desired location in the computer.

- One month data must be preserved.

section: Service and Maintenance of Photoelectric Smoke Detectors
text:
4.1.2.7. Service and Maintenance Photoelectric Smoke Detectors (point-type smoke detectors)
The "Maintenance Fault" of analog smoke sensors is generated when there is a fault relating to the analog value of the device. This usually happens when the device fails calibration. For calibration to fail it generally means that the device has become too contaminated to be compensated for and requires maintenance.

The OEM recommends removing the device from its base and connecting it to the handheld programmer (TCH-B200), which will confirm the analog value.
- The analog value is typically in the low 60s when the sensor is clean.
- A higher analog value indicates contamination requiring cleaning.

Cleaning Procedure:
1. Turn over the device.
2. Place the Outer Cover Removal Tool over the base of the device so that three of the cut-outs sit over the metal terminals.
3. Push down on the handle of the Removal Tool to release all four clips. Pull the two halves of the device apart, exposing the smoke chamber cover.
4. By twisting the Removal Tool anti-clockwise, the Removal Tool can be carefully lifted off from the device.
5. Remove the chamber gently and clean using an Air Detector Duster. The wire mesh can also be removed for cleaning.
6. After cleaning - The wire mesh smoke chamber cover can be reassembled and the two halves can be joined together by aligning the arrow and the outer cover rib, and pushing down until they snap tight.

Note: According to the OEM recommendation, the smoke chamber should be replaced every 36 months.

text:
4.1.2.8. Standard Test Protocol for Automatic Smoke / Fire Detection System

Alarm Thresholds:
Stage 1 - Action: 0.6 ± 0.05 % obs/m, Delay 30 seconds
Stage 2 - Fire: 1.6 ± 0.05 % obs/m, Delay 45 seconds

1. Check the Automatic Smoke / Fire Detection System in the Driver Cab (DTC), Doorways, Passenger Area, Lavatories, and Electrical Cabinet / Panel.

Stage 1 - Action indications to check:
- Blinking Indication Light on the Control / Detection Panel of the affected coach.
- The TCMS Driver Display Unit in the Driver Console/Desk in DTC will display the fire detection indication symbol in Yellow Color and the corresponding coach number diagnostic message.

Stage 2 - Fire indications to check:
- The TCMS Driver Display Unit in the Driver Console/Desk in DTC will display the fire detection indication symbol in Red Color and the corresponding coach number diagnostic message.
- The MIN 1 FD lamp at the MCP Unit Display Panel of the Driver Console/Desk in DTC will be illuminated.
- The FDS Buzzer will be activated in the Hooter/Buzzer Panel of the Driver Console/Desk in DTC.

2. Test self-diagnostics capability: electrical discontinuity, air flow obstruction, system disability/faults.
3. Test buzzer activation in passenger area via FDS ENABLE switch.
4. Verify all detection zones respond correctly.

title: Maintenance Manual for FSDS and FDSS Volume-1 (Vande Bharat & Amrit Bharat Coaches)
text:
4.1.2.9. Air Flow Monitoring
The HOCHIKI FIRELINK 25 monitors the airflow of the aspirating system in the unit, ensuring that the system remains operational and sensitive to smoke detection.

Fault Indications:
- A fault indication is triggered and a Low Flow Error is recorded in the data log if the airflow value falls below the Low Flow Limit Parameters, which may suggest a blocked inlet pipe.
- A fault indication is triggered and a High Flow Error is recorded in the data log if the airflow value exceeds the High Flow Limit Parameters, which may suggest the pipe network has developed a leak.

Air Flow Test Procedure:
a. Equipment: Use a calibrated anemometer to measure the normal airflow value (Fn) by placing it approximately 30 cm before the first sampling point in the pipe network.

b. Parameters:
- Normal Flow (Fn): Determined from the sampling configuration
- Test Flow Rate (Ft): Ft = Fn ± 10% for testing the airflow monitoring
- Low Flow Fault: Triggered when flow falls below Fn - 20%
- High Flow Fault: Triggered when flow exceeds Fn + 20%

c. Procedure:
1. The normal airflow (Fn) (Lt./min.) shall be determined from the sampling configuration used for the fire test with the help of application software or anemometer.
2. The aspirating smoke detection unit under test shall be tested at the test flow rate (Ft) (i.e. Ft = Fn ± 10%) for testing the airflow monitoring.
3. For an aspirating smoke detection unit under test that has a memorized normal flow, the Fn shall be entered into the memory in accordance with normal operating instructions for the detection unit.
4. Reduce the airflow to the low flow limit (Fn - 20%). Verify that a Low Flow fault indication is generated.
5. Increase the airflow to the high flow limit (Fn + 20%). Verify that a High Flow fault indication is generated.

text:
4.1.3. Do's and Don'ts

DO's:
1. Use appropriate PPE (masks, protective clothing) while changing dust separators/filters.
2. Follow the maintenance schedule strictly.
3. Maintain proper records of all maintenance activities.
4. Check LED indications on the detection panel regularly.
5. Verify that cleared sampling points detect smoke properly after cleaning.
6. Download data log as per schedule.
7. Use only OEM-recommended spare parts and consumables.

DON'Ts:
1. Do NOT reuse dust separators/filters.
2. Do NOT operate the system with the front cover removed.
3. Do NOT remove wires when the system is powered.
4. Do NOT use solvents for cleaning the detection panel. Use only isopropyl alcohol and lint-free cloth.
5. Do NOT perform hard reset without proper procedure (use MENU > Password > RESET).
6. Do NOT ignore recurring faults - investigate root cause.
7. Do NOT allow untrained personnel to access or modify the system.

text:
4.1.5. Troubleshooting

SN 1: Smoke not detected
Possible Cause: Aspiration sampling point(s) blocked.
Solution:
- Excessive dust accumulation can block the sampling point. Use a hole suction gun or a vacuum cleaner to clean the blocked point(s).
- Note: Check smoke detection for the cleared sampling point to ensure its proper functioning.
- Vandalism: Visible sampling points (e.g. in lavatories) may be blocked due to vandalism. Check for obstruction by tapes, paper, wooden pieces, etc.
- Use a hole suction gun or a vacuum cleaner or air compressor to clean the blocked point(s). After cleaning, check the smoke detection for the cleared sampling point to ensure its proper functioning.
- If the sampling point is still not detecting smoke, check the detector for isolation or malfunction. Seek OEM guidance if needed.

SN 2: Air Flow Error
Possible Cause (Low Flow): Choked filter / Obstructed sampling pipe or sampling points.
Solution: Replace the choked filter. Clear the obstructed sampling pipe or sampling points.

Possible Cause (High Flow): Loose capillary / Loose pipe joints / Broken inlet pipe / Missing end cap.
Solution:
- Refit the loose capillary. Proper fitting of the capillary to be ensured.
- Tighten the pipe joints.
- The inlet pipe if found broken or cracked, needs to be replaced.
- Provide an End Cap in the sampling pipe. Ensure it is fixed properly.

SN 3: False Alarm
Possible Cause: Aspirating Smoke Detection Unit setting is required.
Solution: Seek guidance from the Supplier/OEM.

section: FDSS Technical Details - Aerosol Fire Detection and Suppression System
text:
5. FIRE DETECTION AND SUPPRESSION SYSTEM (FDSS)
5.1. Aerosol Fire Detection and Suppression System for Amrit Bharat Coaches and Vande Bharat Chaircar Coaches (Ver. 2.0)

5.1.1. Technical Details
The Aerosol Fire Detection and Suppression System, on activation rapidly releases aerosol to extinguish the fire, thereby preventing damage to the coach and equipment.

Key constructional features:
1. Aerosol Generator: The core component where the aerosol is produced. It typically contains a solid aerosol-forming compound.
2. Thermal Activation Device: This device activates the aerosol generator upon reaching a specific temperature, initiating the production of the aerosol.
3. Mounting Hardware: Brackets and supports that secure the aerosol generator and other components in place.

The aerosol is produced in a generator that is activated by a thermal device when the required temperature is reached. It suppresses the fire through a combination of chemical and physical mechanisms without harming the environment.
The aerosol is an ultra-fine component that remains suspended in the area, offering protection against re-ignition and facilitating easy cleanup. These units are compact and eliminate the need for costly pressure vessels, nozzles, and distribution piping.

title: Maintenance Manual for FSDS and FDSS Volume-1 (Vande Bharat & Amrit Bharat Coaches)
section: Types of Thermal Activation Devices - FDSS
text:
5.1.1.1. Types of Thermal Activation Devices

I. Bulb Thermal Actuator (BTA)
The BTA combines both detection and activation for a single condensed aerosol generator. When a fire occurs, the temperature inside the enclosure reaches a pre-selected detection temperature, at this temperature the BTA's bulb bursts, mechanically activating the generator.
Components: 1-Bulb, 2-Mechanical Part, 3-Activator, 4-Safety Pin, 5-Assembled BTA
OEM: FIREPRO (Activation Temperature: 93°C)

II. Thermo Cable / Cord
The thermo cable typically consists of a heat-sensitive material. This material is engineered to trigger the aerosol generator upon reaching the designated temperature, causing it to release the fire-suppressing aerosol.
Components: 1-Thermo Cable, 2-Actuating Device
OEM: PYROGEN (Activation Temperature: 100°C)

III. Manual/Thermal Activation Head
This activation device is designed to activate the aerosol generator either manually or thermally.
a. Manual Activation: Allows the user to manually initiate the aerosol release by pulling out the pull-pin.
b. Thermal Activation: Automatically activates when it detects a specific temperature.
Components: 1-Activation Head, 2-Pull-Pin
OEM: STAT-X (Activation Temperature: 95°C)

text:
II. Aerosol Generator with BTA Activation (FIREPRO)
Installation Procedure:
1. Before installation, inspect the integrity of the aerosol generator.
2. Observe installation parameters as per manufacturer's recommendations (Table-8).
3. Position the mounting bracket and securely fasten it to the cabinet or wall.
4. Fasten the fixing bracket on the body of the aerosol generator, around mid-height.
5. Assemble the two BTA parts by screwing the threads clockwise.
6. Connect the adapter to BTA by turning it clockwise.
7. Unscrew the thermo connector cover from the generator unit by turning it anticlockwise.
8. Connect the BTA to the thermal interface of the generator unit by turning it clockwise.
9. Remove the safety pin from BTA after completing the installation.

Caution: The safety pin on the upper part of the BTA must only be removed when the system installation is complete, not beforehand.
Note: The safety pin will be needed for later circumstances or maintenance, so it is advisable to tie it on a wire strand and leave it hanging from the body of the BTA. Insert the safety pin back into the BTA if the system is disassembled, moved, or adjusted for any reason.

title: Maintenance Manual for FSDS and FDSS Volume-1 (Vande Bharat & Amrit Bharat Coaches)
text:
III. Aerosol Generator with Thermo Cable Activation (PYROGEN)
Installation Procedure:
1. Before installation, inspect the integrity of the aerosol generator.
2. Observe installation parameters as per manufacturer's recommendations (Table-8).
3. Paste double-sided tape on the aerosol generator for clamps. Now tie clamps on double-sided tape.
4. Position the mounting clamps and securely fasten them to the cabinet or wall.
5. Install the thermo cable with the actuation device using a cable tie.
   - Use at least one stainless steel cable tie at the end of the thermo cable.
   - For mounting the in-between section, nylon cable ties or stainless steel cable ties can be used.
6. Now connect the actuation device to the aerosol generator.

Caution:
- Do not forget to paste the double-sided tape under the clamps.
- Do not cut the thermo cable.
- Do not heat the thermo cable.
- Do not mount the thermo cable near the heated item.

Note: The aerosol generator should be mounted vertically; however, for space constraints, the generator can be mounted horizontally (installation parameters as specified in Table-8 should be maintained).

title: Maintenance Manual for FSDS and FDSS Volume-1 (Vande Bharat & Amrit Bharat Coaches)
text:
IV. Aerosol Generator with Manual / Thermal Activation Head (STAT-X)
Installation Procedure:
1. Before installation, inspect the integrity of the generator. It should not be damaged.
2. Observe installation parameters as per manufacturer's recommendations (Table-8).
3. Position the mounting bracket and securely fasten it to the cabinet or wall.
4. Securely attach the generator to the mounting bracket with the generator clamp, taking care to ensure the clamp is free of the initiator mechanism and that all bolts are securely tightened.
5. Position generator, via the bracket-mounting swivel, to allow for an unimpeded discharge upon activation.
6. Install the activation head on the generator by screwing it with hands. Ensure that the screw thread is not crossed during tightening.
7. The hole on the activation head should be fully or partially visible after hand tightening.

Caution:
- Care must be taken so that the generator does not directly discharge at close range at the wall, ceiling, horizontal, or vertical surfaces of the equipment.
- Aerosol generators must never be positioned to discharge directly at each other.
- Pulling the pull pin of the activation head will discharge the generator.

title: Maintenance Manual for FSDS and FDSS Volume-1 (Vande Bharat & Amrit Bharat Coaches)
text:
5.1.1.5. Post Fire Maintenance
1. After discharge, allow a minimum agent holding time of 10 minutes before ventilating the hazard space.
2. Always have backup portable fire extinguishers on hand for use in the unlikely event of fire re-ignition.
3. Ventilate the hazard area thoroughly by forced ventilation or by opening doors and windows.
4. Inspect that all fires have been extinguished and that there are no localized hot spots or other sources of re-ignition present.
5. Any minor amounts of agent residue not removed during ventilation should be thoroughly vacuumed, blown, brushed, or washed away (as appropriate).
6. Exhausted aerosol generators will remain quite hot to the touch after discharge. They can be removed by wearing suitable hand protection.

Caution:
- Do not touch aerosol generators within 15 minutes after the end of the discharge. The generator metal surfaces may be hot enough to cause injury to unprotected skin.
- Ensure the fire is completely extinguished before ventilating the hazard space.
- Ventilate thoroughly or use a self-contained breathing apparatus before entering.
- For areas with sensitive electronic equipment, recovery activities should begin immediately after system discharge and the area is secured from fire re-ignition.

   Stage 1 (Action): LED and Flasher light activated on fire detection panel, Yellow symbol on TCMS DDU, corresponding coach diagnostic message.

   Stage (Fire): Red lamp ON on driver desk, Red symbol on TCMS DDU, coach diagnostic message.

   (i) Electrical discontinuity: Indication on detection panel of affected coach.
   (ii) Obstruction in air flow (blockage/breaking/opening of sampling pipe): Fault on detection panel.
   (iii) System disability (switch off fire detection panel): Communication failure fault on TCMS DDU.

4. Buzzer in passenger area: Driver to manually activate buzzer of passenger area after detection of Stage 2 (Fire) on DDU and stopping of the train.

title: Handbook on Wheel Slide Protection Device (WSP)
text:
1.1 Introduction
 LHB coaches have been introduced in services on some of the
 premier trains on Indian Railways with state of art features.
 One of the important feature provided in these coaches are
 WHEEL SLIDE PROTECTION DEVICE (WSP).
 Initially, coaches turned out by production units were having
 two types of WSP’s namely supplied by (a) M/s Knorr Bremse
 India limited & (b) M/s SAB WABCO India ltd. During initial
 supplies Parrizi type processor was received with M/s Knorr
 Bremse air brake system whereas Sab Wabco with its own.
 During further developments, railways started using processors
 manufactured by M/s Knorr Bremse with its own air brake
 system & in the mean time, M/s Faiveley has taken over M/s
 Sab Wabco. Therefore, presently railways is having three types
 of processors (WSP’s) in service:
 1. M/s Knorr Bremse India Ltd.
 2. M/s Knorr Parrizi India Ltd.
 3. M/s Faiveley India Ltd. (earlier known as M/s Sab
 Wabco)

title: Handbook on Wheel Slide Protection Device (WSP)
text:
After introduction in services, it is noticed that, performance of
 WSP specifically Knorr Parrizi system was not up to the mark
 & even firm was not able to give service support due to poor
 response from the OEM. In view of above, Parrizi type WSP
 are being replaced with Knorr Bremse system. Presently,
 railways is having mainly two types of WSP System.
 WSP control unit is a combination of various electronic cards.
 This unit is housed in electrical control panel units. This unit is
 connected by means of various cables through various
 equipments
1.2 Working Principle
 During the course of brake application, there are possibilities
 of skidding/sliding/locking of individual axle. In these cases
 adhesion between the rails & wheels plays vital roll. Above
 situations are likely to cause damage to wheel sets with
 increased braking distance. The main purpose of using the
 WSPs is to utilize the available adhesion. The WSPs provided
 in the system avoids wheel sliding, also cuts the maintenance
 cost. Speed sensors, the part of the system detect the speed of
 the wheel & sends signal to the processor unit.
 The processor unit evaluates the received signal from speed
 sensor of the vehicle & generates signals enabling the dump
 valve/antiskid valves to control the brake cylinder pressure in
 case of any locking/skidding. The control on the brake cylinder
 pressure is instantaneous to the wheel to rail adhesion, keeping
 the wheels within their optimum range of skidding.
 The WSP has some of the major parts.
 1.2.1. Speed Sensor.
 1.2.2. Phonic wheel.
 1.2.3. Microprocessor.
 1.2.4. Dump valves.
 1.2.5. Pressure switch.

title: Handbook on Wheel Slide Protection Device (WSP)
text:
1.2.1 Speed Sensor:
 The speed sensors are fixed on one end of the axle box cover
 with the help of two bolts. During fitment the gap between
 sensor probe & phonic wheel plays vital role. The gap can be
 adjusted with the help of shims & measured through the
 peephole in axle box cover. The other end of the speed sensor
 i.e. cable is connected to junction box in car.
 The sensor system provided on coaches is based on non contact
 type of counting of RPM. This is ensured with the help of
 phonic wheel & sensor probe fitment with some air gap.
 The main function of speed sensor is to pickup the signals with
 the rotation of phonic wheel mounted on axle end & convey to
 microprocessor.

The air gap between the rotating gear (Phonic wheel) & speed
 sensors probe should be
 Knorr Bremse = 0.4 to 1.4 mm
 Faiveley = 1.5 + 0.5 mm

Criteria gap between speed sensor and toothed wheel

1.2.2 Phonic wheel:
 A phonic wheel is installed on one end of each axle. The
 phonic wheel is a toothed wheel (gear type). The purpose of
 this toothed wheel is to alter the internal inductance of the
 adjacent sensor. The change in internal inductance is evaluated
 as axle speed of various axles on a coach. During fitment,
 concentric movement of phonic wheel should be ensured. The
 eccentric movement of phonic wheel may cause signal errors,
 damage of speed sensor probe.
1.2.3 Microprocessor:
 Microprocessor is the heart of the WSP system. This gathers
 the signals from phonic wheel & speed sensors, evaluates the
 vehicle speed. Moreover, during brake application, it monitors
 & bridges the sharp drop of speed of a particular axle/wheel,
 enabling the dump valve to control/adjust the brake cylinder
 pressure.

1.2.4 Dump valve/Anti skid valve:

 dump valves are a type of solenoid valves, connected with the
 air pressure line of brake cylinder. Dump valve/antiskid valve
 should be fitted close to the brake cylinders. These dump
 valves allow to deplete the air available in brake cylinder line
 during brake application based on the signals from WSP
 microprocessor.

 The sensor system provided on coaches is based on non contact
 type of counting of RPM. This is ensured with the help of
 phonic wheel & sensor probe fitment with some air gap.
 The main function of speed sensor is to pickup the signals with
 the rotation of phonic wheel mounted on axle end & convey to
 microprocessor.

The air gap between the rotating gear (Phonic wheel) & speed
 sensors probe should be
 Knorr Bremse = 0.4 to 1.4 mm

 A phonic wheel is installed on one end of each axle. The

 this toothed wheel is to alter the internal inductance of the

 as axle speed of various axles on a coach. During fitment,
 concentric movement of phonic wheel should be ensured. The
 eccentric movement of phonic wheel may cause signal errors,
 damage of speed sensor probe.

 the signals from phonic wheel & speed sensors, evaluates the
 vehicle speed. Moreover, during brake application, it monitors
 & bridges the sharp drop of speed of a particular axle/wheel,
 enabling the dump valve to control/adjust the brake cylinder
 pressure.

 some time on the move and disappeared again in the
 meantime (e.g. loose contacts), are displayed as number

 Train operators are fully aware of the problems resulting from insufficient wheel/rail adhesion when
 a train is accelerating or braking.

During a constant braking force application, dependent upon the coefficient of friction available at
 the wheel/rail interface, the wheel sets could start to slide. Sliding causes damage to the wheel sets
 (flats) and increases the stopping distance.

Technological advances in the area of microelectronics and the use of microcomputers enable the
 WSP function of a braking system to be enhanced by maximizing the use of the available adhesion.
 In addition, benefits can be gained by widening the function and by improving the diagnostics. The
 latter assists in cutting the costs of the maintenance work.

Based on long experience of rolling stock micro electronic systems, the rack version of AEF G2
 WSP control unit was developed. This system is able to make optimum use of available adhesion
 when braking, thereby optimizing the stopping distances and preventing locked (sliding) wheels and
 the resulting damage.

4.1 Architecture Overview
 Axle speed of rotation is measured and evaluated separately within a speed range of 2 to 400 km/h.
 Axle speeds are compared with a reference speed which is a calculated value based on the real axle
 speeds. The comparison between these speed signals determines whether or not an axle is about to
 enter in to a slide mode. The axles speeds are measured via speed sensors and phonic wheels, all
 located at the axle ends.

Solenoid valves (dump valves) are connected to the brake pipe close to the brake cylinders but
 mounted on the underside of the car body. These valves control the increase and decrease of the air
 pressure in the brake cylinders to assure the optimum pressure in the brake cylinders and maximized
 braking for the prevailing wheel/rail interface conditions, and thus prevent sliding from occurring.

4.2.1 Power Supply G2+VD
 The allowed battery voltage is Vbatt = 72 ÷ 110 VDC ± 30%. Tolerances and fluctuations according to EN
 50155:2007-07, interruptions of voltage supply according to class S2.
 The power supply generates 3 different outputs voltages with following characteristics:
 ▪ VA = 5,1 VDC ± 2%;
 ▪ VB = 18 VDC ± 10%;
 ▪ Vout = 24 VDC ± 2%.
 VA and VB are distributed through the motherboard to all boards (CPU + I/O).
 The Vout voltage is connected externally to WBI boards to supply the dump valves.
 The power supply is with automatic power off/on (stand-by) functionality for battery power saving.

4.2.2 WBI boards (WBI_1 & WBI_2)
 The function of WBI board is to control and manage the WSP functionalities. It is composed by two sections:

▪ Speed input section:
 The board has 4 speed input channels to measure the individual axle speeds. The board provides
 isolated 15 V to supply the sensors.
 Each speed channel is equipped with control circuits to check if the sensor is connected,
 disconnected or damaged.

▪ Dump valve drive section:
 The board has 4 digital output channels to drive the dump valves with open/short circuit protection.
 Each WBI board can control two dump valves; each control channel is organized in two outputs: fill
 and vent.
 The fill stage is controlled by a hardware watchdog that determines the maximum valve excitation
 time (9.7 ± 0.2 s).
 Therefore, each channel is monitored by:
 o An interlock circuit to avoid that the vent valve is energized alone (forbidden condition);

o A Life signal that enables the power supply of the channels only if the software is working
 properly (safety condition).

 marked with the designations 1-4 and the speed sensors and phonic wheels are indicated by G1 -

/// 3. AEF G2 WSP System Maintenance
 3.1 Description of the equipment

The WSP control unit is used to provide anti-slide control for complete train or single coaches.

Figure 1: ISO symbol

Figure 2 : Front view of WSP System

The WSP control unit is composed by a 19”rack unit with a mother board mounted on the back side
 and a set of plug-in cards that can be inserted and extracted without dismounting the rack.

The rack is fitted with fixation points that allow installing it into the supporting structure.
 The front panel of the display plug-in unit of the WSP control unit contains a four-digit alphanumeric
 display for the local indication of errors. The errors buffer can be browsed using the four
 pushbuttons.

3.2 Maintenance
 This device doesn't require any maintenance. It is recommended to perform the manual test once in
 every three months at least (refer to the Part 1 of this manual for WSP/system technical description
 for performing the details of manual test).

In case of failure the WSP unit must be repaired by qualified personnel in authorised workshops.
 3.3 Installation and Removal procedure

Caution! Electric equipment! Prior to accessing to electric parts, make sure the power is
 duly switched off.

3.3.1 Removal procedure
 o Ensure that the unit is powered off by tripping the circuit breaker (not supplied within this unit).
 o Disconnect the power supply connector.
 o Disconnect the other connectors by unscrewing the fixing screw.
 o Unscrew the M6 mounting screws, take care to disconnect the earth connection.
 o Remove the WSP unit.

 The Dump Valve is used to prevent the wheel blocking in situations of low adhesion between wheel

text:
WSP system for LHB coaches

Salient features

WSP device fitted to the vehicle has the role of reducing excessive wheel sliding resulting from
 brake applications in situations where wheel / rail adhesion is temporarily impaired and prevents
 wheels from locking / skidding.
 Safe protection of all wheelsets from locking even in the face of extremely low
 adhesion due to wet leaves on the rails.
 Makes good use of the wheel / rail adhesion by regulating brake force.
 Allows short stopping distances by improving the mean coefficient of adhesion.
 Low air consumption
 Low power consumption

Meets the requirements of UIC Code 541-05 and is listed in the UIC appendix L as approved
 system.

The wheel slide protection (WSP) system has evolved from KNORR BREMSE’s
 proven experience in the field of microprocessor-based “wheel slide control". The control units are
 based on Electronic System for Railway Applications (ESRA) technology.

text:
WSP system for LHB coaches

Working principle of WSP – Control Loop

The wheel slide protection (WSP) system forms a closed loop through the brakes and
 wheel set.

The speed sensor detects the speed of the wheel without physical contact and sends a
 proportional frequency signal to the control unit.

The control unit evaluates the frequencies from all of the vehicle’s speed sensors and
 generates signals enabling the anti-skid valve to control the brake cylinder pressure.

The gradient for decreasing or increasing the brake cylinder pressure can be lowered by
 “pulsing".

The control loop adjusts the brake cylinder pressure to the instantaneous wheel-to-rail
 adhesion, keeping the wheels within their optimum range of slip and ensuring maximum
 possible brake force transmission.

MB04 Board

Wheel slide protection i.e. acceleration and slip control, is implemented entirely on board MB04.
 It contains all the electronic peripherals for individual wheel slide control at up to four wheels or
 wheel sets. The anti-skid valves are powered by 24V from board MB04. MB04 has a man-
 machine interface (MMI) integrated into its front panel.
 Man-machine interface
 MGS2 has a man-machine interface (MMI) integrated into its front panel. The MMI peripherals
 comprise:
 − a 9-pin Sub-D female connector for the RS232 interface (to connect a service terminal),
 − a 4-character alphanumeric display, and
 − 4 control keys.

text:

Anti-skid valves

The anti-skid valve works as an actuator in the wheel slide control loop, and is activated by the
 control unit.

The anti-skid valve is designed to reduce the brake cylinder pressure step by step whenever

source: Knorr-Bremse Group, 14th CMG Meeting PURI, September 2014, Rajiv Agarwal
text:
WSP system for LHB coaches

Speed sensors
 The speed sensor scans a ferromagnetic rotating gear (tooth module / Phonic wheel) that is centered
 over the axle. It works without physical contact and does not wear. The frequency of the digital current
 signal is directly proportional to the circumferential speed of the rotating gear. When the vehicle is at
 standstill, the output current from the sensor assumes the value ( low & High ).

The control unit monitors the speed sensors for correct operation at both standstill and on the move.
 Open circuits and faults to ground are identified. The electronic part of the speed sensors withstands
 short-circuiting, prevents reversal of its polarity and resists EMC interference. Rotating gears with 80
 teeth are used as standard.

1 – Speed Sensor Open / Short Circuit. (Check wiring of speed sensor, wiring is either open or short

WSP system for LHB coaches

WSP checking procedure at Sheds / Depots / Workshops

Check WSP display (in MB04 Card at WSP panel placed in power panel of coach) before start of
 maintenance.

WSP display ‘99’ means system is healthy. Other testing need to be followed (Dump Valve Self Test
 by pressing ‘S2’ switch), if required.

WSP display ‘95’ means present status is healthy but system has logged previous fault and system is
 serviceable. To check the previous fault please follow following steps :

Press ‘S1’ switch display for less than 3 Sec. Display will show in following sequence : 8888-95-
 7201(/7301)-0301-A1F101-A2F201-…..-95. Note down the failure code coach wise and date wise.
 Take corrective measure in respective areas.

Proceed with other testing (Dump Valve Self Test by pressing ‘S2’ switch).

DON’T press ‘S3’ switch (to clear volatile fault memory) and let the coach run with 95 code. But
 ensure that the required repairs is done for the fault which is showing / logged.

Follow the same procedure in next maintenance or testing. Record & check if any new fault is logged.

WSP system for LHB coaches

WSP checking procedure at Sheds / Depots / Workshops
 WSP display ‘7201’ or ‘7301’ means there are some current fault logged in system. To check faults
 follow these steps:

Press ‘S1’ switch for less than 3 sec. The display will show in following sequence : 8888-7201 (/7301)-
 0301- A1F101-A2F201-…..-7201 (/7301). Note down the failure code coach wise and date wise in
 log book. Rectify according to fault code (A1F1 , A2F2 etc.).

Check the display whether 95 or 7201 (/7301). If 95 then proceed with further testing. If fault still exists
 then rectify accordingly.

DON’T press ‘S3’ switch (to clear volatile fault memory) and let the coach run with 95 code. But ensure
 that the required repairs is done for the fault which is showing.

Follow the same procedure in next maintenance or testing. Record and check if any new fault is
 showing / logged.

WSP system for LHB coaches

Precautions for reduction of Card Failures
 Card failures mostly take place because of the following

1) High surges in the electric power supply especially because of welding & other equipment's which
 draw very high current. Ensure electric supply to control unit is off while using such equipment's.

2) Disconnecting cards when power is ON & display is “LIVE”. Ensure fuse 63 & 65 are removed so
 that no power supply goes to control unit before removing, loosening or replacing any of the cards in
 the board.

3) In case download is being taken by using an additional SB03A ( part no STN28328) service board /
 can connector, ensure power is off or fuse is removed before fitting or removing the Can card (In case
 Railways uses the ST03 Software).

4) Short circuit in the control panel or connecting wrong wires during repair of any other equipment in
 the control panel which has relevance to control unit provided by Knorr Bremse. Railway electricians
 to take precautions.

5) Loose connections result into sparking & short circuit of card. Railway electricians to ensure proper
 connections.

Precautions for reduction of Speed Sensor failures

In general the speed sensor Gap should be checked every quarter or whenever the fault 12,
 22, 32, 42 is showing in the WSP display. It can be corrected by addition or removal of shims.

The gap has to be maintained between 0.9 mm to 1.4 mm.

In case of damage of the speed sensor, it needs to be replaced. It is not recommended to
 repair the damaged sensor. Kindly use only Knorr make speed sensor. Other make of speed
 sensors may not provide proper input for correct functioning of our WSP.

In case of open or short circuit of the speed sensor fault 11,21,31,41 will show in the display.
 Kindly check the wirings & repair the same. If not repairable then replace.

Phonic wheel

WSP system for LHB coaches

Precautions for reduction of Phonic Wheel failures

1) Ensure correct tightening torque. (As per Alstom manual, Tighten to 21 NM).

2) Ensure proper Quality of Screws & Washers. (As per RDSO instructions to all Zonal
 Railways , M8 size screw to IS 1367 Pt.III Class 10.9 along with spring washer to the IS 3063
 type-B should be used for securing phonic wheel. LOCTITE 243 or equivalent glue should be
 used to ensure rigid connection between internal and external thread).

3) Ensure wheel speed sensor Gap is maintained (Kindly maintain the gap of 0.9 mm to 1.4
 mm. Less gap can result in touching of wheel sensor with phonic wheel & more gap can
 result into incorrect signal from sensor to Control unit).

4) Ensure use of proper tools for tightening / removal. (Kindly use box spanner with proper
 length of extension for tightening the phonic wheel. Use of improper tools / spanners can
 damage the head of the screw).
